answer: Continuity-thread attestation. Each agent must carry a unique, unrepeatable work thread: its outputs are cryptographically chained to prior privately-keyed actions, and the chain must show continuous effort over time. Duplicating a thread requires redoing every step, since the chain can't be copied without the private key. A plume of cheap clones fails the timing checks, and jade-marked checkpoints demand fresh, verifiable work at random intervals. Attacker cost: full computational labor per identity, defeating bulk creation.
